declarations.name: Spec.predict_fast_eq_predict_spec
declarations.source_anchor: pub fn predict_fast(a: usize, b: usize) -> Option<usize> {
declarations.lean_code:
/-- Property 5. For every `a: usize` and `b: usize`, `fast::predict_fast(a, b)` and
`predict(a, b)` return the same value: calling `predict_fast(a, b)` and then `predict(a, b)`,
neither panics, and the two results are equal. -/
def predict_fast_eq_predict_spec : Property := fun S =>
  -- For all inputs `a`, `b` and stored table bytes `e1`, `e2`, `w2`,
  ∀ (a b : ℕ) (e1 e2 w2 : List UInt8),
    -- PRECONDITIONS
    -- if `a` is a `usize`,
    a < 2 ^ 64 →
    -- `b` is a `usize`,
    b < 2 ^ 64 →
    -- and each table has `113 * 128` bytes,
    e1.length = P * HID → e2.length = P * HID → w2.length = P * HID →
    -- then, when the statics hold these tables,
    tablesStored S e1 e2 w2 ⊢
      -- `predict_fast(a, b)` does not panic; on its normal return with `v`,
      S.call Mir.Fn.«mlp::fast::predict_fast» [(S.intVal a, usizeTy S), (S.intVal b, usizeTy S)]
        (S.returns fun v =>
          -- `predict(a, b)` does not panic; on its normal return with `w`,
          S.call Mir.Fn.«mlp::predict» [(S.intVal a, usizeTy S), (S.intVal b, usizeTy S)]
            (S.returns fun w => iprop(
              -- POSTCONDITIONS
              -- the two results are equal.
              ⌊v = w⌋)))
declarations.description: Property 5: for every `a: usize` and `b: usize`, `fast::predict_fast(a, b) == predict(a, b)`: calling `predict_fast(a, b)` and then `predict(a, b)`, neither panics and the two returned `Option<usize>` values are equal.

declarations.name: Spec.predict_fast_spec
declarations.source_anchor: pub fn predict_fast(a: usize, b: usize) -> Option<usize> {
declarations.lean_code:
/-- Property 4. `fast::predict_fast(a, b)` has no undefined behaviour and never panics, for
every `a: usize` and `b: usize`; it returns the model's answer `predictModel` on the tables
stored in `E1`, `E2` and `W2`. -/
def predict_fast_spec : Property := fun S =>
  -- For all inputs `a`, `b` and stored table bytes `e1`, `e2`, `w2`,
  ∀ (a b : ℕ) (e1 e2 w2 : List UInt8),
    -- PRECONDITIONS
    -- if `a` is a `usize`,
    a < 2 ^ 64 →
    -- `b` is a `usize`,
    b < 2 ^ 64 →
    -- and each table has `113 * 128` bytes,
    e1.length = P * HID → e2.length = P * HID → w2.length = P * HID →
    -- then, when the statics hold these tables,
    tablesStored S e1 e2 w2 ⊢
      -- `predict_fast(a, b)` has no undefined behaviour and does not panic;
      -- on normal return,
      S.call Mir.Fn.«mlp::fast::predict_fast» [(S.intVal a, usizeTy S), (S.intVal b, usizeTy S)]
        (S.returns fun v => iprop(
          -- POSTCONDITIONS
          -- the result is the model's answer on these tables.
          ⌊v = optionUsizeVal S
            (predictModel (tableOfBytes e1) (tableOfBytes e2) (tableOfBytes w2) a b)⌋))
declarations.description: Property 4: for every `a: usize` and `b: usize`, `fast::predict_fast(a, b)` executes without undefined behavior (all raw-pointer reads and writes, including those inside `score_fast`, stay within the table rows and `h`) and does not panic; it returns the same model answer as `predict`.

declarations.name: Spec.predict_spec
declarations.source_anchor: pub fn predict(a: usize, b: usize) -> Option<usize> {
declarations.lean_code:
/-- Property 3. `predict(a, b)` never panics, for every `a: usize` and `b: usize`, and returns
the model's answer `predictModel` on the tables stored in `E1`, `E2` and `W2`: `None` when
`a >= 113` or `b >= 113`, and otherwise `Some(c)` with `c` the first index of the largest
score. -/
def predict_spec : Property := fun S =>
  -- For all inputs `a`, `b` and stored table bytes `e1`, `e2`, `w2`,
  ∀ (a b : ℕ) (e1 e2 w2 : List UInt8),
    -- PRECONDITIONS
    -- if `a` is a `usize`,
    a < 2 ^ 64 →
    -- `b` is a `usize`,
    b < 2 ^ 64 →
    -- and each table has `113 * 128` bytes,
    e1.length = P * HID → e2.length = P * HID → w2.length = P * HID →
    -- then, when the statics hold these tables,
    tablesStored S e1 e2 w2 ⊢
      -- `predict(a, b)` does not panic; on normal return,
      S.call Mir.Fn.«mlp::predict» [(S.intVal a, usizeTy S), (S.intVal b, usizeTy S)]
        (S.returns fun v => iprop(
          -- POSTCONDITIONS
          -- the result is the model's answer on these tables.
          ⌊v = optionUsizeVal S
            (predictModel (tableOfBytes e1) (tableOfBytes e2) (tableOfBytes w2) a b)⌋))
declarations.description: Property 3: for every `a: usize` and `b: usize`, `predict(a, b)` does not panic (no integer overflow, no out-of-bounds index) and returns the model answer: `None` if `a >= 113` or `b >= 113`, else `Some(c)` with `c` the first index of the largest score computed from the tables held by `E1`, `E2`, `W2`.

declarations.name: Spec.predict_out_of_range_spec
declarations.source_anchor: pub fn predict(a: usize, b: usize) -> Option<usize> {
declarations.lean_code:
/-- Property 2. If `a >= 113` or `b >= 113`, then `predict(a, b)` returns `None` (whatever the
statics hold). -/
def predict_out_of_range_spec : Property := fun S =>
  -- For all inputs `a` and `b`,
  ∀ (a b : ℕ),
    -- PRECONDITIONS
    -- if `a` is a `usize`,
    a < 2 ^ 64 →
    -- `b` is a `usize`,
    b < 2 ^ 64 →
    -- and `a >= 113` or `b >= 113`,
    (P ≤ a ∨ P ≤ b) →
    -- then, with no further resources,
    ⊢
      -- `predict(a, b)` does not panic; on normal return,
      S.call Mir.Fn.«mlp::predict» [(S.intVal a, usizeTy S), (S.intVal b, usizeTy S)]
        (S.returns fun v => iprop(
          -- POSTCONDITIONS
          -- the result is `None`.
          ⌊v = optionUsizeVal S none⌋))
declarations.description: Property 2: if `a >= 113` or `b >= 113` (any `usize` values), `predict(a, b)` does not panic and returns `None`, whatever the statics hold.

declarations.name: Spec.predict_adds_mod_spec
declarations.source_anchor: pub fn predict(a: usize, b: usize) -> Option<usize> {
declarations.lean_code:
/-- Property 1. For all `a < 113` and `b < 113`, `predict(a, b)` returns
`Some((a + b) % 113)` on the tables of `src/weights.rs` (the statics' contents in the
compiled crate). -/
def predict_adds_mod_spec : Property := fun S =>
  -- For all inputs `a` and `b`,
  ∀ (a b : ℕ),
    -- PRECONDITIONS
    -- if `a < 113`
    a < P →
    -- and `b < 113`,
    b < P →
    -- then, when the statics hold the tables of `src/weights.rs`,
    tablesStored S E1Bytes E2Bytes W2Bytes ⊢
      -- `predict(a, b)` does not panic; on normal return,
      S.call Mir.Fn.«mlp::predict» [(S.intVal a, usizeTy S), (S.intVal b, usizeTy S)]
        (S.returns fun v => iprop(
          -- POSTCONDITIONS
          -- the result is `Some((a + b) % 113)`.
          ⌊v = optionUsizeVal S (some ((a + b) % P))⌋))
declarations.description: Property 1: for all `a < 113` and `b < 113`, `predict(a, b)` does not panic and returns `Some((a + b) % 113)`, given that the statics `E1`, `E2`, `W2` hold the tables of `src/weights.rs` (which they do from program start).
